newsitem.title: LEBANON: BLC bank and Solidere A up in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: BLC bank and Solidere A up in Beirut.

text.p: Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce hit a record high on the Beirut Stock Exchange for the fourth successive day while Banque Audi fell for the third day and Bank of Beirut was unchanged.
Solidere A caught up with B shares, reaching $11 from $10.5. Both shares continued to trade in heavy demand.
Total supply of Solidere on the first fixing was 128,868 -- including only 800 B shares -- against demand for 491,610.
The LIBX bank index fell 0.11 percent to 163.82. The LISPI general index rose 0.39 percent to 89.44 and the BLOM general index rose 2.35 percent to 964.80.
Market turnover rose to 234,777 shares for a value of $2,038,040 from 168,128 shares and $1,942,678 on Thursday.
Among bank shares, BLC rose to $19.625 from $19.5. A block of 8,000 BLC shares traded on the floor at $19.75.

Banque Audi dropped to $25.375 from $25.625. The share touched a high of $26 on Tuesday. The bourse reported on Friday a transaction in which some 30,000 shares changed hands at $25.625 outside the exchange a day earlier.
Bank of Beirut was unchanged at $4.
Of the four listed industrial firms, Ciments Libanais was unchanged at $1.2812 on trade of 1,973 shares.
There was no trade in the other listed shares: Ciments Blancs, Eternit and Uniceramic.
